framework: A toolkit for building and training neural networks. Its main trick is working out every gradient automatically.
PyTorch: The framework most AI researchers use to build and train neural networks, written mostly for Python.
automatic differentiation: Getting gradients without working out formulas by hand: the computer keeps notes during the forward pass and reads them backwards.
computation graph: The web of notes a framework keeps during the forward pass: every number, which numbers it was made from, and how.
tensor: A grid of numbers (a list, a table, or a stack of tables) that a framework does math on, and keeps notes on, as one unit.
optimizer: The part of a framework that nudges the weights once their gradients are known. Adam is the usual choice.
parameter: Any number that training is allowed to change: every weight and every bias.
